notes: Written before the baseline window opened (2026-06-29), and tightened once in between: v1's ink and trim wording is what round 1 of the measurement check caught as ambiguous (kappa 0.61, marginal); the arm's-length and exactly-2mm rules below are the round-2 fix, and two_people_confirmed is checked on the strength of that round-2 kappa (0.86, acceptable) -- the 'two people' in this plan's check are the two raters of print-msa.
metric_name: First-presentation defect rate: daily proportion of orders rejected at the QC desk, both shifts

operational_definition.what_measured: Whether one produced order passes first presentation: all four named checks pass = accept (reject_any = 0); any check fails = reject (reject_any = 1). The daily metric is rejects / orders presented, one subgroup per service day.
operational_definition.how_instrument: QC desk check at the handoff shelf, against the order ticket: (1) paper stock -- ream/SKU label matches the ticket; (2) trim -- within 2 mm of ticket dimensions, desk steel rule, top/middle/bottom sheet (exactly 2 mm passes); (3) ink -- no smudge, streak, or banding visible at arm's length (~60 cm) under the desk lamp on the top sheet or either pull sheet; (4) quantity -- full recount at or under 50 pieces, counting-scale weigh count above 50. Each failed check is one tally mark in the reject log, so an order failing two checks carries two marks but is one rejected order.
operational_definition.precision_unit: Binary per order; daily proportion reported to 4 decimal places
operational_definition.starts_when: The order is staged at the QC desk with its ticket attached
operational_definition.stops_when: Pass: shelved for pickup and the day's presented-count incremented. Fail: red-tagged with the failed check(s) circled in the log, routed to reprint -- logged by whoever found it, at find time, never reconstructed at close

logistics.who_collects: Tessa Nguyen owns the QC desk log on day shift, Omar Haddad on evening; Jordan Pike confirms intake specs on the ticket so the check has something unambiguous to check against
logistics.where_collected: QC desk at the handoff shelf, main production room
logistics.when_how_often: Every produced order, both shifts, 21 consecutive service days (Mon-Sat), 2026-06-29 through 2026-07-22 -- a census of the window, not a sample
logistics.sample_size_rationale: Proportions need a different n arithmetic than means: the engine's sample-size panel (proportion calculator, planning p 0.09 from the Q2 reject log, +/-1.5 percentage points at 95%) returns n = 1399 -- around twelve times the coffee-bar's continuous n=120, which is the teaching point. ~75 orders/day x 21 service days ~= 1,550 clears it, and 21 daily subgroups clears the >=20-subgroup floor for freezing p-chart limits. Checking every order costs 30-60 seconds at handoff, so a census beats sampling here.

bias_note: A census of the window removes pick-the-easy-orders bias, so the residual risks are definitional and seasonal: the definition risk is handled by the two-rater kappa rounds (marginal, then acceptable after the definition fix); the seasonal risk is that this is a summer-session window -- fall-term order mix runs heavier on rush jobs -- so daily counts and order_type are recorded on every row for a like-for-like fall comparison, and the charter carries term start as a named risk.
